One development crosses the notification threshold.

A TMLR-accepted paper submitted September 22, 2026, “Greedy Decoding Is Not Precision-Invariant,” demonstrates that nominally deterministic LLM inference is not reproducible from `(model, prompt, decoding algorithm)` alone. On identical hardware, merely switching BF16 ↔ FP16 caused output divergence on **49–100% of prompts** across six models, four model families, and three benchmarks; a single token difference frequently cascaded into a different trajectory. The authors also derived five intervention predictions and report that all five matched experiment. citeturn2view0

**Exact capability/invariant affected:** computational provenance and reproducibility. This is not a new first-class capability class, but it materially strengthens v0.4's existing invariant that consequential transformations be inspectable and its requirement that rerunnable activities preserve “exact inputs, code or method identity, parameters, environment where material.” The new result establishes that numerical execution semantics are sometimes epistemically material rather than merely implementation metadata.

**Why v0.4 is insufficient as currently written:** v0.4 can represent the phenomenon through its existing computational-lineage/provenance machinery, so no new primitive is justified. The weakness is normative: “environment where material” permits an implementation to omit numerical precision/backend details because the specification does not identify them as reproducibility-critical. The experiment shows that omission can make two apparently identical deterministic audit runs produce different claims or reasoning trajectories. In FAR, that can propagate into extraction, evidence selection, inference, adjudication, or synthesis.

**Minimal architectural change:** do **not** add a capability class. Tighten the existing computational-lineage contract so consequential model executions record, when applicable, at least model/artifact hash, inference implementation/version, numeric precision or quantization mode, hardware/backend and materially relevant kernel/runtime configuration, decoding parameters, and determinism controls. Reproducibility claims should be scoped to that execution environment rather than treating greedy decoding as intrinsically deterministic. Where exact replay matters, validation should test replay under the recorded environment or explicitly report cross-environment instability.

The other new material I screened—including SEMV's provenance-bearing contestation/memory consolidation, Agentic-IC3's verifier-gated semantic proof search, TwinCheck's counterfactual tool-call verification, and loss-tolerant quantum spacetime attestation—fits existing v0.4 extension points for challenges/updating, formal assurance, inference validation, and provenance/attestation respectively. None clears v0.4's burden for a new first-class primitive. citeturn1academia39turn1academia42turn1search14turn1academia40

One previously omitted argument-validation paper merits inclusion: **a verifier cannot enforce a property the representation never declares**.

This is an overlap-based omission check, not a replay of missed executions. Drive still does not expose the October catch-up report or JSON ledger, so exact ledger-level deduplication remains unavailable.

### On the LLM Verification for Argument Graph Generation

**Jakub Bąba and Jarosław A. Chudziak — October 19, 2026, arXiv:2610.27361v1.** [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27361v1).

**Experiment and evidence status.** The authors converted 112 human-annotated microtext graphs, injected 404 single structural defects, and compared an exact deterministic validator with Gemini 3.7 Flash across three calls per graph. The LLM attained 96–100% “detected at least once” rates, but objected to 11/112 structurally correct graphs, changed its verdict on 6.2% of identical inputs, and had roughly 2,758-ms median latency versus approximately 1 ms for the validator. **Evidence: author-observed bounded experiment plus deterministic checking on declared structural properties—not a machine-checked theorem or independent replication.** genui{"citation":{"ref":"turn446view0"}}

The sharper result concerns specification coverage: statement types, proof standards and polarities were closed enumerations and were never violated; argument scheme was only a free string, producing 27 non-taxonomic assignments across 24/112 graphs. Neither verifier detected them because no permitted vocabulary had been formally declared. genui{"citation":{"ref":"turn446view0"}}

**Proposed, not demonstrated end-to-end.** The paper recommends deterministic structural validation, followed by solver evaluation of formal argument semantics, then LLM review or debate only for contextual properties. However, its solver tier was analyzed rather than implemented or experimentally evaluated. Results use one small corpus, one schema and one model; the graphs contain only three to ten nodes. genui{"citation":{"ref":"turn446view0"}}

**FAR obligation implicated — my assessment.** CORE-010 must preserve not only a graph but its declared vocabulary, closed/open-world status and ownership of each validation obligation under fixed \(L,J,I\). Exact checking of represented constraints cannot establish validity for omitted constraints. This complements *Argument Graph Uncertainty*: uncertainty propagation cannot repair an unspecified admissible-value set.

**Strongest alternate/subsuming explanation.** Conventional schema validation and design-by-contract fully explain the demonstrated failure. The paper does not establish a new argumentation theorem or a distinctive FARA necessity; its value is a clean assurance counterexample separating checker exactness from specification completeness.

**Single executable next test.** Define `scheme` initially as an unconstrained string and submit a structurally valid graph containing `scheme="supports_somehow"`. Require FAR to report **structure valid; scheme-vocabulary obligation unspecified**, not “graph verified.” Then replace the field with a closed enumeration and require deterministic rejection of the unchanged graph.

Nothing selected materially challenges **PROJECT-FAR-CORE-THEORY-1.1**. FAR-CORE-004 remains contract-free **MINIMALITY impossibility**, not universal sufficiency impossibility. FAR-CORE-010 retains exact theory indexed by \(L,J,I\) and frame-subtracted residue indexed by \(\Gamma\). The 14 bounded Lean formalizations establish neither global universality, I3 independent replication, priority, commercial performance nor moat. No global saturation is claimed.
